title: runtime: fastpath gating + precision-toggle safe-mode for KV cache & batching fallbacks
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: fast-path kernel selection and aggressive precision/quantization toggles provide measurable throughput gains, but they've been the root cause of subtle correctness regressions in edge workloads (long-tailed sequences, KV cache boundary cases) and occasional instability in continuous batching. This PR introduces a runtime-level 'safe-mode' and per-request fastpath gating that trades a small amount of peak performance for predictability and correctness when heuristics indicate risk. 

What this change does (high level):
- Add per-request fastpath gating based on: model precision compatibility, KV cache validity, and batch composition heuristics. Requests that fail gating are routed to the conservative execution path.
- Introduce a precision_toggle feature flag and a runtime-safe-mode (global + per-deployment) that disables speculative precision switches and aggressive kernel fast-paths.
- Harden KV cache lookups: add an explicit validation step for cached prefix/tensor shapes at the boundary between cached and non-cached segments to avoid mismatched-kernel assumptions. Fallbacks now occur earlier and with clearer telemetry.
- Scheduler/batcher tweaks: when a request is routed to the conservative path we ensure batching buckets preserve ordering and avoid mixing incompatible precision lanes; this reduces requeue churn and improves tail latency under mixed workloads.
- Add E2E and unit tests covering KV cache boundary mismatches, precision toggle behavior, and batching fallbacks.

Why this approach: previous attempts to micro-optimize kernel selection caused hard-to-trace failures in production (see SUP-402). Rather than removing the optimizations, we gate them so teams can opt-in per deployment or per-request, and we ensure graceful fallback behavior that preserves correctness and provides better observability for future tuning.

Rollback/fallback plan: the runtime-safe-mode is configurable via feature flag and configmap; if we see regressions we can set safe-mode=true at the deployment level without code rollback. The change introduces no DB migrations and is opt-out for existing deployments (default keeps prior behavior unless safe-mode enabled by ops).

review_comments: Diego Morales: Can we avoid per-request heap allocations in the gating path? The current impl does an allocation for the gating vector on hot paths.
Ava Chen: Addressed — switched to an arena-allocated smallvec and added benchmarks showing negligible overhead (see new test in batcher_bench).

Priya Nair: KV cache validation sounds good, but we need to ensure the extra validations don't regress p99s for cache-hit dominated workloads. Can we gate validations behind a sampling flag for the first rollout?

Ava Chen: Added sampling-based validation in cache_manager (10% by default) and a config knob in runtime_config.yaml. Full validation can be enabled in safe-mode. Benchmarks included in PR show p99 impact < 0.5ms for sample-enabled mode.
Samir Patel: We should add a metric for 'fastpath_gated' reasons (precision|kv_mismatch|batch_incompat). Also ensure tracing spans include the gate decision for replay debugging.
Ava Chen: Added counters and tracing span tags. Updated observability checklist and dashboards (docs/runtime-safe-mode.md).
ci_checks: benchmarks: stable (no regression in median; small p75 improvements)
merge_summary: Merged by Diego Morales (squash and merge). Commit message consolidated to: 'runtime: safe-mode + fastpath gating to improve correctness for KV cache and mixed-precision workloads; add validation, scheduler separation, and rollout docs.'
release_notes: Added runtime-safe-mode (feature flag) that disables speculative precision fast-paths and enables conservative KV cache validation. New per-request fastpath gating and metrics added to help diagnose precision/kv fallbacks. Safe-mode can be enabled at deployment level via runtime_config.yaml.
